concepts.title: Mutable vs Immutable + id()
concepts.code:
a = "hi"
print(id(a) == id(a))

nums = [1, 2]
before = id(nums)
nums.append(3)
print(id(nums) == before)   # same object, sirf andar change

s = "hi"
s = s + "!"                 # naya string object bana

concepts.title: print()
concepts.code:
print("Hello, Python!")
print("Age:", 22)
print()              # khaali line
print("Bye")

concepts.title: f-string Formatting Tricks
concepts.body: {value:.2f} decimal places, {value:>8} right align, {value:,} comma separator, {value:.1%} percentage.

concepts.title: Concatenation
concepts.body: Do strings ko + operator se jodna.
concepts.code:
first = "Hello"
second = "World"
print(first + " " + second)

concepts.title: Strings are Immutable
concepts.code:
s = "hello"
try:
    s[0] = "J"
except TypeError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

s = "J" + s[1:]
print(s)          # naya string

concepts.title: format()
concepts.body: String ke andar { } placeholders me values insert karta hai. Purana tarika hai; f-string usse better hai.
concepts.code:
name = "Ashu"
age = 22
print("My name is {} and age is {}".format(name, age))
print("{1} is {0}".format("cool", "Python"))

concepts.title: startswith()
concepts.code:
text = "hello world"
print(text.startswith("hello"))
print("report.pdf".startswith(("data", "report")))   # tuple bhi chalta hai

concepts.title: if statement
concepts.code:
age = 20
if age >= 18:
    print("You are an adult")
print("Done")     # ye hamesha chalega

concepts.title: Ternary Operator
concepts.body: if-else ko ek line me likhne ka tarika: value_if_true if condition else value_if_false.
concepts.code:
age = 20
status = "Adult" if age >= 18 else "Minor"
print(status)

concepts.title: Truthy & Falsy Values
Combining Conditions & in
concepts.code:
day = "Sat"
if day == "Sat" or day == "Sun":
    print("Weekend")

if day in ("Sat", "Sun"):        # chhota tarika
    print("Weekend again")

age, has_id = 20, True
if age >= 18 and has_id:
    print("Entry allowed")

concepts.title: pass Statement
break
else with loop
enumerate()
concepts.body: Loop me item ke saath uska index bhi deta hai. Ab i = 0; i += 1 likhne ki zarurat nahi.

concepts.title: zip()
concepts.code:
names = ["A", "B"]
ages = [20, 25]
for n, a in zip(names, ages):
    print(n, a)

concepts.title: List Comprehension
concepts.code:
squares = [x * x for x in range(1, 5)]
print(squares)

# Loop wala lamba tarika (same result):
squares2 = []
for x in range(1, 5):
    squares2.append(x * x)
print(squares2)

concepts.title: Alias vs Copy (Important!)
concepts.body: b = a naya list nahi banata, ek hi list ke do naam ban jate hain. Ek me change karoge to dusre me bhi dikhega.
concepts.code:
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a               # alias (same list)
c = a.copy()        # asli copy

b.append(99)        # a bhi badal gaya!
print(a)
print(c)            # c safe hai

concepts.title: append()
concepts.code:
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]
fruits.append("mango")
print(fruits)

fruits.append(["x", "y"])     # poori list ek item ban gayi
print(fruits)

concepts.title: pop()
concepts.code:
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "mango"]
item = fruits.pop()
print(item)
print(fruits)
print(fruits.pop(0))      # pehla item
print(fruits)

concepts.title: clear()
concepts.body: List ke saare items ek saath hata deta hai. List khaali reh jati hai.
concepts.code:
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]
fruits.clear()
print(fruits)

concepts.title: sorted() vs sort()
concepts.body: sort() list ko badal deta hai aur None deta hai. sorted() original ko chhode bina nayi sorted list deta hai (kisi bhi iterable par).
concepts.code:
nums = [3, 1, 2]
new = sorted(nums)
print(new)
print(nums)
print(sorted("python"))

concepts.title: Stack (LIFO) using List
concepts.body: Stack = last in, first out. Plates ki pile jaisa. append() se push, pop() se pop.
concepts.code:
stack = []
stack.append("a")
stack.append("b")
stack.append("c")
print(stack.pop())    # c pehle nikla
print(stack.pop())
print(stack)

concepts.code:

print(point)
print(type(point))

rgb = 255, 128, 0      # bracket ke bina bhi tuple
print(rgb)

concepts.title: instance method
class variable
concepts.code:
class Car:
    wheels = 4                  # class variable

    def __init__(self, brand):
        self.brand = brand      # instance variable

c1 = Car("Tesla")
c2 = Car("BMW")
print(c1.wheels, c2.wheels)
Car.wheels = 6                  # sabke liye badla
print(c1.wheels, c2.wheels)

concepts.title: class method
Core Concepts
concepts.tip: Error handling should be specific, readable aur observable. Except Exception blindly mat use karo.
concepts.code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

p = Path("profile.json")
data = {"name": "Ashu", "role": "AI Engineer"}
p.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

loaded = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
print(loaded["role"])

concepts.title: Core Concepts
Interview Depth
concepts.body: Is page ka goal hai concept ko implementation decision tak le jana. Interviewer ko syntax se zyada reasoning, edge cases aur trade-offs dikhte hain. Har concept par 4 sawal tayyar rakho: WHAT (kya hai aur kab use karoge), WHY (kaunsi problem solve hoti hai), RISK (common bug / failure mode kya hai), TRADE-OFF (simple option aur scalable option me kya difference hai).

concepts.title: Advanced topics (second pass)
concepts.body: __str__ users ke liye readable text deta hai; __repr__ developers ke liye exact representation (debugging aur lists me). Is page ke baaki advanced topics: dataclass, isinstance() / issubclass() aur @property. Pehli reading me inhe skip karke dusre round me karo.
concepts.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Student:
    name: str
    marks: int = 0

s = Student("Ashu", 95)
print(s)
print(s == Student("Ashu", 95))

concepts.title: Core Concepts
concepts.code:
def project_answer(problem, approach, result):
    return (f"Problem: {problem}. "
            f"Approach: {approach}. "
            f"Result: {result}.")

print(project_answer("manual support workflow",
                     "API + webhook + validation",
                     "less manual repetition and better traceability"))
